statement: Four blocks A, B, C and D are compared on a balance. A and B together exactly balance C and D together. A and C together are heavier than B and D together. A and D together are lighter than B and C together. Which block is the heaviest?

choices.misconception: I read the third weighing the wrong way round, as if A and D together were heavier than B and C.
I read the second weighing the wrong way round, as if A and C together were lighter than B and D.
I read both of the unbalanced weighings the wrong way round.
I thought weighing pairs can never single out one block, so I did not combine the weighings.

hints: Compare the first weighing with the second. Which two blocks swapped pans?
Combine the weighings. Going from the first to the second, B and C swap pans; going from the first to the third, B and D swap. Each swap shows which of two blocks is heavier.

First to second: the pan that gets C instead of B becomes heavier, so C is heavier than B. First to third: the pan that gets D instead of B becomes lighter, so D is lighter than B. Then use A + B = C + D to compare A with C.

solutions.reliable: Start from the balance A + B = C + D. In the second weighing, B and C have swapped pans, and the pan holding A now tips down, so C is heavier than B. In the third weighing, B and D have swapped pans compared with the first, and the pan holding A now rises, so D is lighter than B. So C is heavier than B, and B is heavier than D. Finally, A + B = C + D and B is heavier than D, so A must be lighter than C to keep the balance. Therefore C is heavier than all the others. The transferable idea: compare two weighings that differ by one swap, and the swap tells you which of the two blocks is heavier.
solutions.elegant: Write the first weighing as A + B = C + D. Adding the second weighing's inequality to it shows A > D, subtracting it shows C > B, and the third weighing compared with the first shows B > D. Then A - C = D - B, which is negative, so C > A. C is the heaviest.

whyOnTest: Balance puzzles reward combining weighings: two weighings that differ by one swap compare the swapped blocks directly.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
